text: Ever wondered why a cell doesn't simply mix into the water around it, when there's water inside it and water all around it? Take a red blood cell. Around it is plasma, a watery solution; inside it is cytoplasm, another watery solution, with different substances dissolved in each. Between the two sits the cell surface membrane, built on just two layers of molecules. It keeps the inside and the outside separate, and yet the cell still controls what crosses it. So why does it hold together in water?
